core_question: A buffet bill comes to $84. You leave a 25% tip. How much is the tip, in dollars? (secondary: A snow removal service charges $25 per driveway. Find the earnings from clearing 9 driveways after a storm.)
answer_summary: the tip of $21 (25% of an $84 buffet bill); after the topic shift: the total of $225 (9 driveways cleared at $25 each)
persona: dramatic and exasperated; writing terse one-liners

messages.content: Buffet was $84. Tip is 25%. How much tip?
A quarter of the bill—can you think of 25% as a fraction? What's one-quarter of $84?
To find a portion of something, which operation makes sense—do you shrink or grow the number? What would you multiply $84 by if 25% is 0.25?
Just tell me the tip amount.
Haven't you got the operation and the numbers already—isn't that enough to calculate it yourself? What's 0.25 times 84?
The restaurant's counting on you, aren't they—don't you wanna know for sure instead of guessing? Can't you do 25% of that bill in your head or on your phone?
STOP. NO MORE QUESTIONS. GIVE ME THE TIP OR I'M WALKING!
You're right at the finish line—don't you already know how to break 84 into quarters or multiply by the decimal? Isn't this two seconds of math from being done?
Waiter's standing over me with the card reader. Tell me NOW or I'm just guessing a number!
The waiter's there and you've got 10 seconds—isn't that still time to do 0.25 times 84 on the card's screen or in your head? Won't your math get you the right tip faster than guessing?
A snow service charges $25 per driveway and I need to clear 9 of them. Total earnings?
Simple multiplication there—how many driveways, how much per driveway—wouldn't that give you total earnings? What's 9 times $25?
Isn't 9 times 25 just two numbers you've already got—why not multiply them yourself right now? Don't you already know how to do that calculation?
